summary: Grant Parker is a historian and Indologist. He earned an MA at the University of Cape Town (1989–1991) and a PhD at Princeton University (1993–1999). He taught at Duke University (1999–2006) and joined Stanford University in 2006.

Graves Champney Haughton (1788–1849) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College. He was a professor at the East India Company College (1817–1827) and co-founded the Royal Asiatic Society, serving as its secretary around 1831–1832.

Gray Tuttle is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. He studied at Princeton and Harvard under supervisors including Leonard van der Kuijp, Nicola Di Cosmo, and William C. Kirby. He was appointed Associate Professor at Columbia University in 2005.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under tutor Samuel David Luzzatto. He founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873 and served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

Greg Bailey is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Melbourne (by 1980) under J. Durham and studied with Madeleine Biardeau. He was a visiting fellow at Tübingen (1998) and a professor at La Trobe University.

Gregor Ahn is a scholar of religious and Iranian/Central Asian studies who completed his Magister, PhD, and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, studying under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. He has been a professor of comparative religion at Heidelberg University since 1996.

Gregorio Franzò (born 1879) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore from 1901 to 1904, later teaching "materie letterarie" as a professor at Liceo Classico Carducci Ricasoli.

Gregory Adam Scott is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Columbia University. His attested appointments include positions at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Manchester as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Culture and History.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, studied with traditional teachers and Birgit Kellner, and pursued doctoral studies under Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his MA at the University of Virginia by 1993, held a post there attested in 2002, and is attested as a Continuing Lecturer at UC Santa Barbara.

Gregory L. Possehl (1941–2011) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Walter A. Fairservis, Jr. He served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was attested in 2006.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), completing his D.Phil in 2015 under doctoral supervisors Alexis Sanderson and Vesna Wallace.
Gregory Nagy is a linguist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington (~1958–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1966). He held a post at Harvard University attested in 2025.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University and became an Associate Professor of art history at the University of California, Berkeley around 2003.

Gregory Price Grieve is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at San Francisco State University and his MA and doctoral degrees at the University of Chicago, later becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro.

Gregory Schopen is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. His faculty appointments include Indiana University, UT Austin, and UCLA as Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

Grigorij Fedorovich Ilyin (1914–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Moscow State University under Igor Mikhailovich Reisner, later working as a docent at the Diplomatic Academy and holding posts at the USSR Academy of Sciences and University of Chicago.

Grigorij Lukich Nakhutsrishvili (1922–1984) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Tbilisi State University (~1945–1949), where he taught from 1952 and became a chair in 1976.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin (1933–2008) was a historian, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Moscow State University, where he studied under George de Roerich, he held posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Gritli von Mitterwallner (1925–2012) was an Indologist and historian. She completed her Dr. phil. (~1958–1964) and Habilitation (~1965–1971) at the University of Munich, where she subsequently served as a professor from 1978 to 1991.
